steps.title: Lines and angles — rules to know
steps.intro: Most geometry questions are built on these rules. Know them cold.

head: Rule
Value
Remember
rows: four angles at a crossing add to \(360°\)
half of a full circle — a straight line
only if marked with a small square, or given
next to an acute angle sits an obtuse one
Adjacent angles on a straight line
they complete the same angle to \(180°\)
the two angles in its corners are equal
the two angles inside it add to \(180°\)
\(\perp\) to the same line, or \(\parallel\) to the same line
or equal small angles / small + large \(=180°\)
parallel only if given or proved
angles pointing left \(=\) angles pointing right
equal parts: count the gaps, not the points

tips: Letters instead of numbers? Plug in round numbers that look like the figure. Check that the four answers come out different — if two tie, plug in again.
Overlapping angles: add them and subtract the full turn (\(360°\)) or the straight angle (\(180°\)).
A bent line between parallels? Draw a line through each bend, parallel to both. It always works.
Adding angles to \(180°\)? Use the units digit: \(64°+79°+x=180°\) → \(4+9=13\). Therefore, \(x\) ends in \(7\).
Two lines look parallel, but nothing says so? Look for a rule that proves it: two angles inside a U that add up to \(180°\), equal small angles, or two lines \(\perp\) to the same line.

steps.stem: In the accompanying figure, \(a\parallel b\). The marked lines are perpendicular. What is the value of \(x\)?
explanation: \(a\parallel b\), and small angles are equal. At line \(b\), the angle between the transversal and line \(b\) (above \(b\)) is also \(64°\).
The marked right angle is made of this \(64°\) angle and \(x\): \(64°+x=90°\).
Therefore, \(x=90°-64°=26°\). Choice 2.

steps.stem: In the accompanying figure, lines \(a\) and \(b\) are both perpendicular to line \(c\). Line \(d\) crosses lines \(a\) and \(b\). What is the value of \(x\)?
choices: It cannot be determined from the information given.
explanation: \(a\perp c\) and \(b\perp c\). Two lines perpendicular to the same line are parallel. Therefore, \(a\parallel b\).
Now \(d\) is a transversal of two parallel lines. The \(50°\) angle is a small angle, and \(x\) is a large angle.
Choice 4 is the trap: "\(a\parallel b\)" is not written, but the two right angles prove it.

steps.stem:
Points \(A\), \(B\), \(C\) and \(D\) lie on a line in this order, as shown in the accompanying figure.
Given:
\(\begin{cases} AC=11 \\ BD=14 \\ AD=20 \end{cases}\)
What is the length of \(BC\)?
explanation: \(AC\) and \(BD\) overlap on \(BC\): \(AC+BD=AD+BC\).
\(11+14=20+BC\). Therefore, \(25=20+BC\) and \(BC=5\). Choice 3.
Step by step: \(AB=AD-BD=20-14=6\), and \(BC=AC-AB=11-6=5\).

steps.stem: Three adjacent angles form a straight angle. Their measures are in the ratio \(2:3:4\). What is the measure of the largest angle?
explanation: \(2+3+4=9\) units make \(180°\). Therefore, one unit is \(\frac{180°}{9}=20°\).
The largest angle is \(4\) units: \(4\cdot20°=80°\).

explanation: \(p\) and \(70°\) are on a straight line: \(p=180°-70°=110°\).
\(q\), \(r\), \(s\) and \(t\) make a full circle. Therefore, \(r+s+t=360°-55°=305°\).

steps.stem: In the accompanying figure, \(a\parallel b\) and \(c\parallel d\). What is the value of \(x\)?
explanation: \(a\parallel b\) (line \(c\) crosses them): the acute angles are equal. Therefore, the acute angle next to \(x\) at the lower left is \(77°\).
\(c\parallel d\) (the diagonal crosses them): the other acute angle next to \(x\) is \(56°\).
The three angles make a straight angle: \(77°+56°+x=180°\). Therefore, \(x=180°-133°=47°\). Choice 4.
Shortcut: \(7+6=13\), which ends in \(3\). Therefore, \(x\) must end in \(7\). Only \(47°\) does.

steps.stem: In the accompanying figure, four lines intersect at one point. Which expression equals \(x\)?
explanation: The angle next to \(m\) is \(180°-m\), the angle next to \(n\) is \(180°-n\), the angle next to \(k\) is \(180°-k\).
These three angles and \(x\) make a straight angle: \((180°-m)+(180°-n)+(180°-k)+x=180°\).
Therefore, \(540°-(m+n+k)+x=180°\) and \(x=m+n+k-360°\). Choice 4.
Plug in: \(m=n=k=140°\) gives \(x=180°-3\cdot40°=60°\). Choices 1, 2 and 3 give \(240°\), \(140°\) and \(-140°\). Only choice 4 gives \(60°\).

Shortcut · Mirror test: if two letters play exactly the same role in the given, swapping them cannot change the answer, so a choice that changes when you swap them is out. Here \(m\), \(n\) and \(k\) play the same role (three overlapping angles around one point). Swap \(m\) and \(n\): choices 1 and 4 stay the same, but choice 2 becomes \(n-m+k\) and choice 3 becomes \(n-m-k\). They change, so they are out. One plug-in (\(m=n=k=140°\), \(x=60°\)) decides between 1 and 4: choice 4.

steps.stem: In the accompanying figure, \(a\parallel b\). What is the value of \(x\)?
explanation: Draw a line through the bend, parallel to \(a\) and \(b\). It splits \(x\) into two parts.
The upper part makes a Z with the \(36°\) angle. Therefore, it is \(36°\). The lower part makes a Z with the \(62°\) angle. Therefore, it is \(62°\).
Zig-zag rule: \(x\) points right, \(36°\) and \(62°\) point left. Therefore, \(x=36°+62°\).

steps.stem: In the accompanying figure, \(a\parallel b\). What is the value of \(x\)?
explanation: Zig-zag rule: the angles pointing left \(=\) the angles pointing right.
Pointing left: \(40°\) and \(65°\). Pointing right: \(x\) and \(35°\).
Check with parallel lines through both bends: the lower bend splits into \(35°\) and \(65°-35°=30°\); the upper bend splits into \(40°\) and \(30°\). Therefore, \(x=40°+30°=70°\).

steps.stem: Two adjacent angles form a straight angle. Their bisectors are drawn from the common vertex. What is the angle between the bisectors?
explanation: Call the two angles \(2a\) and \(2b\): \(2a+2b=180°\).
The angle between the bisectors is \(a+b=\frac{180°}{2}=90°\).

steps.stem: In the accompanying figure, \(a\parallel b\). What is the value of \(\frac{\alpha+3\gamma}{\beta}\)?
explanation: \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are vertical angles, and \(\beta\) and \(\gamma\) are both small angles: \(\alpha=\beta=\gamma\).
\(\frac{\alpha+3\gamma}{\beta}=\frac{\beta+3\beta}{\beta}=\frac{4\beta}{\beta}=4\).

steps.stem: In the accompanying figure, three lines meet at point \(O\). What is the value of \(x\)?
explanation: The \(114°\) angle and the angle next to it are on a straight line: that angle is \(180°-114°=66°\).
The \(144°\) angle is made of this \(66°\) angle and \(x\): \(66°+x=144°\).

steps.stem: Based on the information in the accompanying figure, what is the value of \(\alpha+\beta\)?
explanation: \(\alpha\), \(43°\) and \(109°\) make a straight angle: \(\alpha=180°-109°-43°=28°\).
\(\beta\) is made of \(43°\) and \(\alpha\): \(\beta=43°+28°=71°\).

steps.stem:
Four different lines are given:
\(\begin{cases} p\perp q \\ q\perp r \\ r\perp s \end{cases}\)
Which of the following is necessarily true?
explanation: \(p\) and \(r\) are both perpendicular to \(q\). Two lines perpendicular to the same line are parallel: \(p\parallel r\).
(Also \(q\parallel s\), since both are perpendicular to \(r\). Therefore, choice 1, \(q\perp s\), is false.)

steps.stem:
Five different lines are given:
\(\begin{cases} c\parallel d \\ d\perp e \\ e\parallel f \\ f\perp g \end{cases}\)
Which of the following is necessarily true?
explanation: \(c\parallel d\) and \(d\perp e\). Therefore, \(c\perp e\). \(e\parallel f\). Therefore, \(c\perp f\) too.
\(c\perp f\) and \(g\perp f\): two lines perpendicular to the same line are parallel. Therefore, \(c\parallel g\).

steps.stem: In the accompanying figure, the line is divided into equal segments. What is the value of \(\frac{x}{y}\)?
explanation: \(x\) covers \(10\) equal gaps and \(y\) covers \(4\). Count the gaps, not the tick marks.

steps.stem:
Points \(A\), \(B\), \(C\) and \(D\) lie on a line in this order.
Given:
\(\begin{cases} AC=17\text{ cm} \\ BD=19\text{ cm} \\ BC=6\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
What is the length of \(AD\) (in cm)?
explanation: \(AC+BD=AD+BC\) (the overlap \(BC\) is counted twice).

steps.stem:
Points \(E\), \(F\), \(G\) and \(H\) lie on a line in this order.
Given:
\(\begin{cases} c=EG \\ d=FH \end{cases}\)
Which of the following is necessarily true?
choices: It cannot be determined from the information given.
explanation: \(c+d=EG+FH=(EF+FG)+(FG+GH)\).
\(EH+FG=(EF+FG+GH)+FG\).
Both sums have \(EF\) once, \(GH\) once and \(FG\) twice. They are equal: \(c+d=EH+FG\).

Shortcut · Plugging in numbers: the points can be anywhere in this order, and a "necessarily" answer must hold for every such line. So test easy lengths. \(EF=1\), \(FG=2\), \(GH=3\): \(c+d=3+5=8\) and \(EH+FG=6+2=8\). Equal, so choices 1 and 3 are out. A second set (\(1\), \(1\), \(1\)) gives \(4=4\) again: choice 2.

steps.stem:
Given:
\(\begin{cases} \gamma+v=180° \\ \delta+4v=180° \\ 0°<v<45° \end{cases}\)
Which of the following is necessarily true?
choices: It cannot be determined from the information given.
explanation: Since \(v>0\), \(4v>v\): \(\delta\) subtracts more from the same \(180°\). Therefore, \(\delta<\gamma\).
Plug in to check: \(v=10°\) gives \(\gamma=170°\) and \(\delta=140°\).

steps.stem: In the accompanying figure, three lines meet at one point. The angles \(u\) and \(v\) overlap on the angle \(y\). Which expression equals \(y\)?
explanation: \(u\) and \(v\) together cover the straight angle once, and \(y\) twice: \(u+v=180°+y\).
Therefore, \(y=u+v-180°\). Choice 3.
Plug in to check: \(u=130°\), \(v=120°\) gives \(y=70°\). Choice 1 gives \(-10°\), choice 2 \(110°\), choice 4 about \(83°\).

steps.stem: In the accompanying figure, \(a\parallel b\). What is the value of \(x\)?
explanation: Zig-zag rule: the angles pointing left \(=\) the angles pointing right.
Pointing left: \(50°\) and \(x\). Pointing right: \(80°\) and \(20°\).
